data.response:
Subject: Meeting Confirmation

Dear [Name],

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to confirm our scheduled meeting, which is set to take place on [Date] at [Time]. 

I appreciate your prompt response and I am looking forward to meeting with you to discuss [meeting topic/subject]. During our meeting, we will dive into [specific agenda items/topics] and collaborate on [goals/objectives]. 

Please let me know if there are any changes or if you have any specific topics you would like to add to the agenda. It is important for us to make the most of our time together.

If there is anything you would like to prepare or any documents you would like to share prior to the meeting, please feel free to send them my way.

Once again, thank you for scheduling this meeting. I am confident that our discussion will be productive and beneficial for all involved.

Looking forward to seeing you soon.

Best regards,
[Your Name]

data.actualMessage: Only 32 times in 158 instances have India completed a successful chases in their Test history. Chennai 1999, Pune 2017, Chennai 2021, Bangalore 2004, 2005, 1987, or most recently Hyderabad 2024; there have been many instances of India failing to handle the fourth-inning pressure at home.
data.subject: Why Shubman Gill and Dhruv Jurel are a throwback to MS Dhoni-Yuvraj Singh

data.actualMessage: On Monday, on a flaking pitch where the ball turned and occasionally kept low, India was struggling. Chasing 192, they were 120/5. Ranchi 2024 seemed like a repeat of the same old story.

data.actualMessage: At the Gabba, he was en route to stardom, but not a star yet. Thus, less baggage. For much of that innings, he had the stability of Cheteshwar Pujara at the other end. Here, he was playing the senior hand.
data.subject: Gill did post a foundation-laying 91 in a historic Brisbane chase. But this was a sterner challenge.

data.actualMessage: The chemistry, but not particularly their methods, whipped up memories of Yuvraj Singh and MS Dhoni when India had just begun to crack the chase code in ODIs. Yuvraj was insouciant, unflustered to a fault, as Jurel was. Dhoni was the puzzle-solver, bending his methods to suit the situation.
